reply.title: The Vertical Throw
reply.story: Standing on the ground, you toss a ball straight up into the air. As it climbs, it slows down until it hangs suspended for a single, motionless instant at its peak before falling back down to your hands. It is easy to watch the velocity change from positive to zero and then negative, but what happens to the acceleration at the very top? Does it stop too, or does gravity keep pulling even when the motion pauses?
reply.cardDescription: Explore how gravity acts on a ball thrown straight up. See how velocity changes while acceleration remains constant at $-g$.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press Play to watch the throw. Observe the velocity and acceleration vectors at different points.
